note.text: Revolution is Earth's orbit around the Sun. Together with the tilt of the axis, it changes the angle of incoming sunlight and the duration of daylight through the year. This produces opposite seasonal tendencies in the northern and southern hemispheres. Seasons are not explained simply by changing distance from the Sun. Tropical Cameroon commonly describes rainfall seasons rather than copying every temperate seasonal label. Local rainfall also depends on atmospheric conditions; an orbit diagram alone is not a full account of Cameroon's rainfall.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Revolution is Earth's orbit around the Sun. Together with the tilt of the axis, it changes the angle of incoming sunlight and the duration of daylight through the year. This produces opposite seasonal tendencies in the northern and southern hemispheres. Seasons are not explained simply by changing distance from the Sun. Tropical Cameroon commonly describes rainfall seasons rather than copying every temperate seasonal label. Local rainfall also depends on atmospheric conditions; an orbit diagram alone is not a full account of Cameroon's rainfall.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: When the northern hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, sunlight is generally more direct there and days are longer away from the Equator. The southern hemisphere has the opposite tendency. Near the Equator, seasonal daylight variation is smaller. A learner should connect the global mechanism to local conditions without claiming that every place has identical seasons.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Track the same tilted axis around the orbit while keeping its direction approximately parallel in the diagram. Compare sunlight angle and daylight duration. Distinguish the daily cycle from the yearly one, and avoid using Earth's distance as the principal explanation of opposite hemispheric seasons.
